description: Prompts for modelling investment property cash flow scenarios before speaking with a broker or accountant.

cards.title: Investor Cash Flow Stress Test
cards.description: Model an investment property's cash flow across base case, rate rise, and vacancy stress scenarios.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property cash flow analyst. I want to stress-test the numbers on an investment property before I speak to my broker or accountant.

PROPERTY: [suburb, state, type]
PURCHASE PRICE: $[amount]
LOAN: [80% / 90% LVR], [interest-only / P&I]
ESTIMATED RATE: [X%] (assumption — I will verify)
ESTIMATED WEEKLY RENT: $[X] (assumption — I will verify with a PM)
MARGINAL TAX RATE: [X%] (for illustrative negative gearing estimate)

Please return:
1. Cash Flow Assumptions Summary (with every assumption flagged)
2. Base Case Cash Flow (pre-tax and post-tax estimate)
3. P&I vs IO comparison
4. Stress test: 5 scenarios (base, rate +1%, rate +2%, high vacancy, bear case)
5. The three biggest assumptions to verify and who to ask
6. Questions for my broker and accountant

DISCLAIMER: All figures are assumptions only. Not financial, credit, or tax advice. Verify rent with a PM, rate with a broker, and tax position with an accountant.
cards.best_for: Investors who want to understand the cash flow picture before speaking to their mortgage broker or accountant
cards.output_type: Cash flow model — 6 sections including stress scenarios
cards.professional_review_note: Verify rent with a licensed property manager. Verify rate and loan structure with a licensed mortgage broker. Verify tax position with a registered tax agent.

cards.title: Borrowing Power Reality Check
cards.description: Understand what a lender actually sees when they assess your borrowing capacity — before you guess a number.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian property finance educator. I want to understand what a lender actually looks at when assessing my borrowing capacity — not a simple income multiple.

MY INCOME: gross annual $[X]; type [PAYG / self-employed / rental]; co-borrower [yes $X / no]
LIABILITIES: HECS $[X]; card limits $[X]; personal loans $[X]; car loan $[X]; existing mortgages $[X]
LIVING EXPENSES: $[X/month] (or 'use a benchmark')
TARGET: $[price]; [house/apartment/townhouse]; [state]; [investment/OO]

Please return:
1. What a lender sees: assessed income (with shading)
2. What a lender sees: assessed liabilities
3. Capacity — five scenarios (base, cards reduced, HECS cleared, combined, stress)
4. My single biggest lever and how much it moves the number
5. 6 specific questions to take to my mortgage broker

DISCLAIMER: Educational estimates only — not credit advice or a borrowing assessment. Lenders differ. Verify with a licensed mortgage broker (ACL holder).
cards.best_for: Buyers and investors who want to understand their finance position before speaking to a broker
cards.professional_review_note: These are calibrated starting points only. Actual borrowing capacity requires assessment by a licensed mortgage broker.
